Love the game! Really well done rogue like. Every run manages to feel fresh enough even when I am using the almost same build.

The game is pretty fun and the story is engaging. Some extra variety or randomness in either the type of enemy, the maps, or the objectives of a given encounter would go a long way. Some of the maps, especially early on, make the runs feel really really repetitive. Once you get past the first zone there is enough variety from things that unlock to make it more engaging, but the static map-enemy-objective combinations don't do the game any favors.

有肉鸽内容的回合制战略游戏。 难度还行，每局游戏时间有点长。 主要打法就是多战斗刷技能升级，最简单的方式就是留一个敌人，然后全队疯狂刷回复或者BUFF技能，一直到出疲惫DEBUFF为止，快的话第一张图就能差不多十级，第二张就能满级，后面就好打多了。 作为肉鸽来说，缺点比较多，最典型的就是随机性过高，但强化的强度却有限。 最典型的就是某个遗物，效果是降低最大血量10点，然后每次战斗后加最大血量，但这个遗物加血量只有20点上限，就非常无语。 BOSS战前没有固定配回复，路上也没有什么地图，只能走一步看一步。 升级给了垃圾技能，花钱刷之后，竟然又是这几个技能，简直无语。 最终BOSS非常恶心，能输出的时间只有一个回合，还会不断招小怪+自己隐身，突出一个赖皮。 翻译问题比较多，各种口口口，建议完善一下字库。
实际内容只有第一关，后面都是加点数值重复

How to use the heroes, what the heroes do in a battle, how to move and how to fight never change. What we are doing is to repeat the similar battle (which is not so interesting) again and again.

I can't quite put my finger on it, but the tactical battles are just not fun, zoc mechanic is weird and I still haven't figured it out, enemies randomly decide to attack my squishies while right next to my tankier guys with no consequences. So, instead of real tactics, or using environment/los you just end up trying to find a position where they can't reach you. On this note, the maps are non existent, a few bumps and some water holes don't qualify as a combat map. You need stuff like high low ground, los elements and more visual variety. The game would be much more fun if the partnership effects were more pronounced so you could actually use them in combat instead of getting them randomly and that rarely. As it stands, for me at least, combat needs quite a few changes to make it work. The rest of the game is fine, I like the art and the rogue lite aspect is OK, not all games need a story/campaign. If the fights were fun I'd play more. May check back in the future. Ps Laurent range is ridiculous, he's supposed to be wizard but has the range of a spearman?

This game was great until I understood a problem with the core mechanics. XP and Health are both gained by using abilities in the combat stages, and abilities have no resource cost. It results in rewarding players for wasting time, you want to stall combat stages to spam abilities for maximum xp and full heal every time. There needs to be a resource limit for abilities or some other fix. I beat the game with all challenges enabled, but it was tedious and not fun because I wasted time in every combat stage to gain advantage. Two major updates later (I played Nov 2025, writing review March 2026) and this problem is still not addressed in patch notes. I can't continue playing.

This game is fun and I love the turn-based tactic mixed with the roguelike aspect... except for one main thing which is why I leave a negative review : the exp. To get exp, which gets you better stat and better skills (the base of the progression system), you're required to do an action. And since the only limits on skills are cooldowns, this incentive you in wasting time healing or buffing yourself. Or attacking with your weak unit first and killing with your stronger one so both get exp instead of being efficient and killing it with you stronger one and letting your weaker unit wait or better position itself. You end up doing "bad" strategical choices to get stronger faster, which ends up making stronger. That's a bad design for a roguelike.
流程太短，玩法单一，完全不值那个价。

The game itself is okay, but it made some design choices that just ruin the roguelike experience. The most important one: Ingame you have to keep choosing if you want your next fight to reward you with perma-rewards for your next playtrough, or stuff for your current run. This makes it feel like a sad, long (3+hour per run) grind that doesnt respect the players time. This forces you to just pick that option a few times, knowing you will lose your run, to unlock stuff to help you. There is NO need for that mechanic, as games can just reward you for how far you went in your run, so you can always choose the 'fun' option, of choosing stuff to help you in your current adventure. Even though the game plays great, im getting bored and don't look forward for my next 3 hour repetation of the same slow fights which I'll 100% percent win anyway. 5/10. Edit: I forgot to mention a 2nd design choice thats bad: rewarding slow and boring gameplay. As you keep your health in the next battle, its encouraged to keep falling back and healing, before engagign in combat. This makes even the easiest of battles boring, because you have to keep making them twice as long as neccecary, to make sure you start your next battle with full health. And yes, you unlock passive healing in the skilltree after like 10 hours of gameplay, but its still boring and annoying and there's no reason to design it like this.

To start with the positives, I like the story, writing, and art style. The game doesn't introduce characters too quickly. It's good that there is an option to speed up animations during combat, which many games of this type do do not have. However, I don't recommend buying this game on the whole. First, your health carries over between battles, and healing is limited, EXCEPT during a battle via healing spells and abilities. It's silly. If my party has multiple healers with unlimited uses, why wouldn't they use that outside of combat to fully heal between battles? Instead, you need to root, stun, or just run away from the last enemy on a mission until your healing spells regenerate, then kill them and end the mission. While you can't do this every mission, it's logically inconsistent that the rest mechanic exists at all. Healing between missions means you have to give up some alternate reward so you're basically punished if you don't exploit this strategy. Another thing that bothers me is there is limited explanation of the skills, abilities, and attributes in the game. So I am forced to make permanent decisions on what rewards to chose, but I don't know for the most part what the rewards actually do. This is a common problem with many games and I don't understand why. Ultimately this leads to you making bad choices that loses you battles. Doing so means you have to start over from the beginning. Which in this game is really tedious because it can take an hour to get through a single map, with repetitive fights to reach the boss. Your characters die in 1-3 hits, and enemies will always try to kill whoever they can. Since you are outnumbered 2:1 or more every battle it's hard to keep this from happening. While there are zones of control, the zones of control don't work in a clearly predictable way the way they usually do in other games. In this game enemies can just step back even when engaged, then use their full movement anyway. So I might move a caster near an enemy, end that character's turn, thinking in a later character's turn I can stop enemies from reaching my character using a melee character's friendly zone of control. Then find out too late the enemy had enough movement points to just walk around anyway. While there is an undo, it's limited to 3 times per battle. In summary, while to a certain extent I like this game, I don't like being punished with a long slog for issues that are not my fault. The developer could have fixed this by letting the player redo unlimited times per turn rather than redoing entire battles, for example. Then if I couldn't predict zone of control I could just try again in a different spot. Also, adding tooltips would have helped with understanding.

The game is overwrought with several different currency mechanics for the runs. The skill pool feels super small, and even though it expands open, that expansion is slow (not to mention skills often do very little different things to just "hit enemy"). The defense weakness system is annoying to track since it's not easy to easily remember your own content for each character. The reason it works in fire emblem is that it's easy to track the weapon triangle. Finally, the story feels generic and overwrought with poorly written dialogue.

虽然写了推荐游玩，但是只是推荐给追求高难度的战棋硬派玩家。 推荐指数：★★★☆☆/★☆☆☆☆（战棋玩家/非战棋玩家） 轻度战棋代餐，依旧存在SRPG与肉鸽的不可兼容性问题，目前游戏玩家也偏少，几乎没有讨论热度。游戏优化很好，pc和steamdeck没有发生任何bug。 个人游玩93个小时，通关20次，外循环的解锁要素强度完全可以覆盖当前挑战难度。所以，游戏在常规难度的重复游玩价值不高，游玩时长20小时以内的玩家会普遍反馈游戏没有难度、重复度很高、物料。 7级试炼（终极试炼）锁8级敌精通及以上难度有一定挑战度，适合硬派老战棋玩家挑战。但其实通关最高难度时，也只有第2章节会有内循环等级资源跟不上敌人强度的问题，在熟练机制后，前期和最终boss都不算难。

WOW, just wow, These games, Lost Eidolons, could've been great, I wanted them to be great. I'm only leaving 1 review for both games, cuz like the developers I'm being lazy. I truly had high hopes for these games, but the 1st is incomplete, at best and the 2nd is 'die forever until you win'. Instead of naming them LE, they should've called them Epic Frustration 1 and 2. I could go into great depth why you shouldn't buy these games, suffice it to say, that when they provide an 'Undo' button, with many chances, save scumming is already written into it. Ah Hell, forget spoilers, be forewarned, the 1st game you will lose some characters, OUTSIDE BATTLE, no matter how well you did in the battle. Then you need to scramble to replace them, which is impossible unless you know it's coming. But don't worry, as i've already said, in the 2nd game, dying over and over and over and over and over and over and over is what you're supposed to do. AND, in both games the rules don't apply to the 'bosses'. In summary, high hopes dashed by lazy devs. So sad. 幻灵降世录女巫的面纱游戏评价： 首先作为战棋策略类游戏，画面质感不错延续了第一代的风格，音乐过场都在线。 系统设计非常有创意，跳出了传统战棋的王道剧情模式，初上手有点难以理解，但通过两次远征大致也就清楚了。 人物剧情和第一代幻灵降世录有关联，看得出制作组野心很大，后续应该是一个系列，人类，历史，幻灵……应该是个可比肩火纹的系列游戏，非常不错，值得期待！！当然现在还为知言早。 如果再引入类似英灵殿～北欧女神，诸神，人类和诸神的对决，哈哈，那就太爽了！ 说回这款游戏本身，有很强的策略性，肉鸽元素也很强，非常好，我玩战棋游戏，长期都有这就完了？不够啊的感觉，这款应该能上百小时。 战棋游戏系统构造相对来说都是比较简单且容易上手的，剧情方面自己体会，重要的是所有对话和选择仔细看完串联起来，整个游戏各方面都不算突出，但放在战棋游戏这个小类别里还是可以算是优等生的，打折绝对值得推荐！ 通关了几次远征后觉得有点无聊了，剧情还是短板，肉鸽元素让人没有继续下去的动力，个人建议：其实每次远征后人物等级和职业技能及金钱和装备都可以保留，（人物等级最高99级，职业等级10级，每阶段职业等级对应增加一个被动技能，）各种状态，圣物，技能，物品，这些重置，装备系统保留并多样化，每个部件可以设置5个品级，每个等级进阶要合并同阶段同样5件装备才行，掉落装备只掉落最低等级的，最高品质的装备还能升级，最高9级，升级逻辑和升品级一样，设个隐藏BOSS，人物等级满级，装备等级满级才会出现。取消难度选择和试炼选择，直接最高难度。 把地图做大，取消回朔，改为手动存档。另外，此游戏游玩必须在线但不需要连机，因为每次远征都会由内置AI系统，完全重置随机生成地图。 肉鸽不是问题，但有目标和成长性的肉鸽才有持续的动力，否则通关个几次，任谁都不想继续了！ 最终试炼挺难的，本身难度不大，难的是随机性，这个本来想详细说说，后来觉得没必要！走到这一步的玩家都有自己的见解，就不班门弄斧了。 终极试炼对新手只有四点建议： 1、前排必须有能抗的角色，不一定能打，但必须要能抗。如果实在不喜欢，那么主角必须转刺客，两个刺客隐身挡路。 2、天国召唤这个技能必须要有。 3、觉得技能这些升级时不合适，危机事件损失过大，不用犹豫，退出游戏到主界面重来便是。 4、第一章最难，过了第一章人物技能属性起来了，就不难了，耐心一点。 最后总结，作为一个独立版本的游戏是不合格的，但作为一个系列的序章是合格的，接下来就看看这个系列如何发展了，期待！ 最后，手柄完全适配，我是在steamdeck上玩的，掌机放心入。

This is a good game --and I feel like there is an amazing game just inches away. The art style is fantastic, the dialogue is fun, powers feel great as you grow through a run, and the characters are multi-dimensional with excellent voice acting... If you've played Fire Emblem, this is going to scratch an itch. I found the combat pretty easy, and I only lost 2 runs through my entire playthrough. The story is where it gets complicated: I loved a lot of it. The pacing of your MC's story is great, you get rewarded with new content after every run. Your companions' stories are also great ... but those take much longer to unlock, and unfortunately don't feel worth pursuing given how long runs go (even on the shortcut mode). My biggest issue with the game overall is the ending, spoilers ahead. [spoiler]The true ending does not feel satisfying. Reconciling with family does not resonate with me as a player in the same way as finally stopping the final boss would have. It boggles my mind that I am supposed to assume that we win sometime after the events of the game... why couldn't we continue the roguelike continue another way than never being allowed to win?[/spoiler] A fun game overall, and close to being a new favorite of mine. Ultimately, I'm going to keep an eye on this studio! I really want to see what their next game looks like, because I see a lot of promise here.

[h2]It is a tentative recommendation, based primarily on the comparison to the previous game. The sequel is an RNG-heavy (Rogue-lite) tactical game in a fantasy setting.[/h2] Something I can't help but admire, it's when the sequel is significantly better than the original game. In the particular case, [b][i]Lost Eidolons: Veil of the Witch[/i][/b]. The developers addressed the issues I had with the first [i]Lost Eidolons[/i] - they culled the small talk and fetch quests, made the characters distinct and good-looking, and even added helmets and character customisation (granted, only name, gender expression, and skin colour, but it is progress). The combat encounters are also more varied and challenging, while the character skill progression has a good pace. While it is still just a tactical game with a linear story and some optional content, now with RNG in the mix, it is, nonetheless, enjoyable. There are difficulty options, fairly frequent auto-saves (on every area transition, though the OS file management system has to be used for the save file management), rebindable controls, adequate system requirements, and skippable animations. There are also persistent upgrades (most things reset between expeditions due to the game being a Rogue-like) and a limited ability to replay the previous battles. The soundtrack does not seem to have any vocal tracks, but it fits the game well and is quite pleasant to listen to. As a part of its RNG nature, the ending does taste a bit sour (i.e., there is no resolution for the main conflict, as one of the developers mentioned, it gets resolved off-screen), as well as the mindless grind it becomes, should one wish to get all story-related events or achievements.

This is a turn-based tactics RPG, overall well produced and has good presentation with its professional artwork and polished UI. The story is OK, the characters are interesting and the dialogue is well written, with even lots of decent voice acting for the main scenes. The SFX design is good, while the music is forgettable. The gameplay is mostly divided in two parts: 1) Out of combat, you proceed in a roguelite manner similar to Darkest Dungeon or Slay the Spire, or any other node based game really. That is, you embark on expeditions with 5 characters, and in between each combat encounter, you're presented with a random set of choices of "nodes" or paths to progress through, where each node offers different rewards/effects/loot, some nodes are camps to rest, others have unique events, that kind of thing. 2) The battles and the tactical combat itself, which is the bulk of hours played, is highly inspired by the Fire Emblem series. That is, mostly exploiting weapon/armor advantages, and low hit-counts to kill any given unit, including your own. But it has some twists tough with special skills and passive skills. All in all this works decently enough, but my main issue is that ultimately these expeditions end up feeling quite repetitive and grindy, and the breadth of different combat encounters does start to feel less and less rewarding on repeated runs. And the grindy feeling come from the utterly small increments that you get in terms of character stats, both whitin an expedition, and also for the overall meta progression. It seriously felt like the same design principles as those predatory mobile or gacha games, you know those types of games where you have to farm tons of different kinds of currency like gems or whatever to then expend them to earn some little reward, then go back to farm again. To be clear, this here is purely a single-player game, so that grind is much lower comparatively. I then research the developers of this game and they are indeed korean, so now I understand where the design patterns are coming from. My main point is that the game should have been focused on being either a full roguelite (like Darkest Dungeon, Slay the Spire, FTL, etc) with deeper and better character and combat customization and variety, OR it should have been more of a traditional cRPG such as Baldurs Gate, with a more standard RPG focus, and then focusing more on its interesting characters, story and setting. It tries to do both things at the same time, but in my opinion, the way it's implemented here ends up feeling... maybe not exactly flat, but just "okay". As it stands, this is a "jack of all trades, master of none" situation. I liked the game well enough, but it does leave you feeling like with different design choices, this game could have been great instead of just alright.

TL;DR: A tactical roguelite with excellent combat, a strong narrative, and meaningful progression that successfully translates the Lost Eidolons formula into a new genre. The setting, themes, art direction, character designs, and music are all excellent. The darker fantasy aesthetic returns while carving out its own identity. There is plenty links to the first game, with a swap to an anime aesthetic. The narrative involves amnesia and adds to the roguelite structure. Its lore is tightly connected to the first game while telling a more focused story with a smaller cast of characters. Partnership levels return and give relationships meaningful long-term progression. An open-world camp is swapped for a selection skin which allows quick navigation between interactions to reduce downtimes. The roguelite elements are well implemented. Head out on expeditions with a party of five characters, encounter random events that can reward or punish along the way. Characters have unique interactions during these events that help mitigate some of the randomness. Acquire relics that dramatically alter builds and strategies. Characters do not regain health between battles, which forces carefully management of resources throughout an expedition. Character levels and weapon enchantments reset after each run, providing the familiar roguelite loop. Combat remains largely unchanged from the first title. The biggest improvement is abilities with cooldowns, which encourages more use. The armor and weapon triangle remains satisfying, while attacks from different angles and the Zone of Control system continue to add tactical depth. Characters have two weapons to adapt to different enemy types and battlefield situations. Larger enemies act like puzzles with multiple randomly assigned weaknesses that reward planning. After each expedition, upgrade at the altar and characters in the tavern while pursuing the many collectibles and milestones. These unlock passive benefits and additional resources to give every run a sense of progression. The tower adds modifiers to future runs.

I am happy to report that the second game in the series did not try to suck all the fun out of my gaming! If you are coming here straight after finishing (or trying to finish) the first game, you will find they share the same setting and basic combat system, some of the characters, but little else. This game lacks the comprehensive (and very long) story arc, but the combat system has been refined and balanced and is generally much better. I found the adjustments in the settings that suited me, and I enjoyably played through this game many times. This game has you do hours-long runs over and over (i.e. Dark Dungeon). After about ten runs, it started to get monotonous. That was still over 80 hours of game play for me. There is still enough back story to tie the theme together, make the transition from the first game, and set the tone for this game. I definitely got my money's worth out of this one!

Played this about 20-30 hours (offline on deck lost me some for my record) and it has a lot of pros but also a lot of cons. First off, it is a legitimate rogue-like strategy RPG in a similar vein of Fire Emblem and props to the dev team for that. However, ultimately the TL:DR is that the balance is wildly all over the place and the battles can get quite tedious, especially when you start scaling up the difficulty (as you are supposed to do) and for boss battles. Pros: - Wealth of progression options that truly do make all of your characters stronger over time - Forgiving system, with the ability to wind back time (to an extent) and by default no serious setbacks if a character dies in a battle (they come back the next battle) - Deep lore + dialogue - Multiple characters to find and recruit - Bond system between characters is both lore based plus also gives combat bonuses in meaningful ways - Many events and options during runs that unlock over time, which help the replayability - Runs great on the Steam Deck Cons: - Combat gets amazingly tedious where any given fight might be your 5 characters vs 20 enemies - Boss fights are so frustrating that they nearly ruin the whole experience, with Fire Emblem Style beast systems where a big enemy requires multiple hits with multiple of the right weapons, which sounds fine in practice until you realize that if you lose one of our your 5 characters in a fight you often can no longer break their defenses. What's worse, is that nearly all bosses will keep spawning adds/extra enemies to fight non-stop - Your characters have a hard cap of level 20, even on hard mode when they need more options - It took 15 hours to unlock a lot of the basic features, like switching classes or before I got my first new characters. The pacing of adding complexity and options felt pretty poor in the beginning. - Runs are quite long for a rogue-like due to the above, with 3-4 hours per run if you are on the later stages - The story is mixed, with some understandable and decent writing followed up by silly nonsense like "that big bad enemy we've been fighting is secretly my family member" Ultimately, I'm right in the middle where I love many aspects of it but as you get further into the progression the slower it can feel and the less satisfying progression is. Do not recommend, but do your research and check it out in depth if you really want to take a stab it.
